summary: Full text of the 2020 Nutrients RCT (51 dyslipidemic adults, Kaneka QH 100 or 200 mg/day, 8 weeks) shows its primary endpoint, brachial FMD, improved versus placebo (+1.3%, p<0.001). This is the narrower endothelial finding Dr. Pham held for source content, so it gets one eligible context; the PK/safety study gets no efficacy credit. A new applicability block limits credit to the cardiovascular (endothelial) surrogate and excludes energy and heart-failure claims, per her rejection of those transfers.

applicability.studied_population: Adults aged 35-65 with untreated mild-to-moderate dyslipidemia and moderate endothelial dysfunction, no cardiovascular disease, given Kaneka QH ubiquinol 100 or 200 mg/day for 8 weeks (PMID 32326664).

population.description: 51 men and post-menopausal women aged 35-65 with LDL-C 130-200 mg/dL, not on statins or other lipid-lowering therapy, moderate endothelial dysfunction (FMD 2.5-6.0%) and no clinical cardiovascular disease; 48 completed.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single-centre, three-arm parallel trial (ACTRN12619000436178), 8 weeks; primary endpoint FMD change at week 8.

dose.administration_frequency: One capsule in the morning and one in the evening with food, 8 weeks (100 or 200 mg/day).
dose.reported_regimen: [100, 200] mg/day; 56 days; one capsule morning one evening with food

normalization.basis: Reported study-material daily dose, not a universal threshold or equivalence to other preparation.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC7231284): Methods 2.1-2.4 (participants, product Kaneka QH and dosing, endpoints, sample size), Results FMD/CoQ10/NOx/oxLDL paragraphs, Funding/COI.

co_therapies: Statins and other lipid-lowering treatments excluded.

outcomes.name: Primary FMD at week 8 increased versus placebo with 200 mg/day (+1.28% +/- 0.90%) and 100 mg/day (+1.34% +/- 1.44%), p<0.001.
Secondary: FMD at week 4 not different (p=0.648); serum NOx increased (p=0.016); LDL oxidation lag time improved with 200 mg/day (p=0.017); plasma oxLDL not different (p=0.905).

limitations: No CVD/heart failure/statin myopathy clinical benefit proved; small population.

FMD is a surrogate; the trial does not show cardiovascular events, heart-failure, statin-myopathy or energy benefit. Signed A006 rejects clinical-outcome and general-energy transfers; credit is limited to this endothelial-function finding.
Small single-centre trial with per-protocol analysis (48 of 51); no FMD difference at week 4. Product supplied by Kaneka; funding from university and institute grants; authors declare no conflicts.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

clinical_review.notes: No efficacy credit: single-blind pharmacokinetic and tolerability study in healthy volunteers, not an efficacy outcome; full text not open access.

limitations: Abstract: single doses of 150 or 300 mg and 4-week dosing of 90, 150 or 300 mg Kaneka QH in healthy volunteers; non-linear dose increases in plasma ubiquinol; no clinically relevant safety findings up to 300 mg. Absorption/safety data, not efficacy.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

source_receipts.title_fetched: Ubiquinol Ameliorates Endothelial Dysfunction in Subjects with Mild-to-Moderate Dyslipidemia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
Study on safety and bioavailability of ubiquinol (Kaneka QH) after single and 4-week multiple oral administration to healthy volunteers.
